purpose: Founder review alternatives only. Names, color palettes, prototype copy, and marks are not official launch identities.
search_method: Limited public web exact-name search; not exhaustive, no official trademark register searched, no domain ownership verification.

excluded.name: Weekmark
excluded.reason: Established brand with foreign trademark registration in multiple service classes

candidates.name: Weekkin
candidates.headline: A little more room to run your business.
candidates.signature: Your business deserves to be heard, even on the busiest week.
candidates.belief: A consistent presence starts with practical human help.
candidates.purpose: Give busy neighborhood-scale businesses a reliable, manageable week of social media support.
candidates.story: Running a small business already asks for a full day. Then there's the public side of it: the update that never gets written, the project people never hear about, and the post sitting in drafts. Weekkin is the idea of a capable extra hand for one agreed week, without turning a small problem into a long retainer.
candidates.voice: Warm, neighborly, observant, complete sentences; no cute baby talk, no fake promises
candidates.mark: paired offset speech tiles with a shared baseline
candidates.visual: Editorial photography of real small-business work, soft cream copy panels, two gently overlapping rectangular speech tiles
candidates.strength: Friendly and independently ownable-sounding word; centers companionship rather than algorithm hacks
candidates.risk: Invented name does not communicate social marketing on its own; needs service descriptor. Search coverage is not legal clearance.
candidates.label: Warm and human

candidates.name: Cadencekeep
candidates.headline: Stay in the conversation.
candidates.signature: One good week of steady, approved communication.
candidates.belief: The habit of showing up is more valuable than a burst of noise.
candidates.purpose: Help small organizations sustain a credible publishing rhythm within a finite, agreed weekly scope.
candidates.story: Every business has something worth saying, but a scattered posting schedule makes it hard for people to notice. Cadencekeep is built around an attainable rhythm: agree what matters, create or manage the approved work, hand back a clearer next week. The goal is consistency, not a promise of viral growth.
candidates.voice: Composed, concise, reliable, businesslike, not agency-jargon heavy
candidates.mark: four offset vertical beats plus a closed continuation line
candidates.visual: Structured cobalt grid, chartlike rhythm motif, acid-lime signal markers, strong sans typography
candidates.strength: Communicates rhythm and long-term consistency; more professional than the first direction
candidates.risk: Slightly long to say and type; compound may not feel elegant to a buyer.
candidates.label: Modern and operational

candidates.name: Weekmorrow
candidates.headline: Make this week matter to the next.
candidates.signature: A useful week of content. A better starting point tomorrow.
candidates.belief: Small consistent acts add up to the presence people remember.
candidates.purpose: Help an owner regain momentum through one scoped week of thoughtful social support and a usable handoff.
candidates.story: The days get busy, and communication slides to tomorrow. Weekmorrow turns that vague tomorrow into one practical week: choose the message, agree on the work and approvals, and hand off something useful. It is about forward progress, not pretending a week can transform a whole company.
candidates.voice: Optimistic, thoughtful, unhurried and plainspoken; no miracle language
candidates.mark: sun crossing a seven-day horizon, two rising lines
candidates.visual: Warm dawn horizon, paper textures made with CSS, calm editorial serif and honest work photography
candidates.strength: Strong narrative arc and possible visual storytelling; future-forward without sounding enterprise-only
candidates.risk: Can sound like a planner or lifestyle brand; may need obvious service descriptor on every page.
candidates.label: Optimistic and story-led

recommendation.reason: The human support story is more differentiated from a generic newsletter. The product descriptor must remain visible to communicate the actual one-week service; candidate still needs independent name clearance.
